# Proverbs 1 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Proverbs-of Solomon son-of-David, king-of Israel:

**2** To-know wisdom and-discipline, to-understand words-of understanding,

**3** To-receive discipline-of prudence, righteousness and-justice and-uprightness,

**4** To-give to-simple-ones prudence, to-young-man knowledge and-discretion.

**5** Let-hear [the]-wise and-let-him-increase learning, and-[the]-discerning counsel let-him-acquire,

**6** To-understand proverb and-enigma, words-of wise-ones and-their-riddles.

**7** Fear-of YHWH [is the]-beginning-of knowledge; wisdom and-discipline fools despise.

**8** Hear, my-son, discipline-of your-father, and-do-not-abandon teaching-of your-mother,

**9** For a-wreath-of grace they [are] for-your-head, and-pendants for-your-neck.

**10** My-son, if they-entice-you sinners, do-not-consent.

**11** If they-say, 'Come with-us, let-us-lie-in-wait for-blood, let-us-lurk for-[the]-innocent without-cause,

**12** Let-us-swallow-them like-Sheol alive, and-whole like-those-going-down-to [the]-pit,

**13** Every precious wealth we-shall-find, we-shall-fill our-houses [with] plunder,

**14** Your-lot you-shall-cast in-our-midst, purse one shall-be for-all-of-us' —

**15** My-son, do-not-walk in-[the]-way with-them, withhold your-foot from-their-path,

**16** For their-feet to-evil run, and-they-hasten to-shed blood.

**17** For in-vain the-net [is]-spread in-[the]-eyes-of every possessor-of wing.

**18** And-they for-their-[own]-blood lie-in-wait, they-lurk for-their-[own]-lives.

**19** So [are] the-paths-of every-one gaining unjust-gain; the-life-of its-possessors it-takes.

**20** Wisdom in-[the]-street cries-aloud, in-the-plazas she-gives her-voice,

**21** At-[the]-head-of [the]-noisy-[streets] she-calls, at-[the]-openings-of [the]-gates in-the-city her-sayings she-says:

**22** "How-long, simple-ones, will-you-love simplicity, and-scoffers scoffing delight for-themselves, and-fools hate knowledge?

**23** Turn at-my-rebuke; behold, I-will-pour-out my-spirit to-you, I-will-make-known my-words to-you.

**24** Because I-called and-you-refused, I-stretched-out my-hand and-no-one attended,

**25** And-you-ignored all my-counsel, and-my-rebuke you-did-not-want —

**26** Also I at-your-calamity will-laugh, I-will-mock when-comes your-dread,

**27** When-comes like-a-storm your-dread, and-your-calamity like-a-whirlwind arrives, when-comes upon-you distress and-anguish.

**28** Then they-will-call-to-me and-I-will-not-answer, they-will-seek-me-earnestly and-will-not-find-me,

**29** Because they-hated knowledge, and-fear-of YHWH they-did-not-choose,

**30** They-did-not-want my-counsel, they-despised all my-rebuke.

**31** And-they-shall-eat from-[the]-fruit-of their-way, and-from-their-[own]-counsels they-shall-be-filled.

**32** For the-turning-away-of simple-ones will-kill-them, and-the-complacency-of fools will-destroy-them.

**33** But-the-one-listening to-me shall-dwell securely, and-shall-be-at-ease from-dread-of evil."

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **1:1**: Mishlei (proverbs) — root m-sh-l carries sense of comparison, likeness, or ruling word. More than mere 'sayings.'

- **1:7**: Reshit (beginning) can mean 'first principle' or 'chief part' — not merely temporal beginning but foundational principle.

- **1:20**: Hokhmot — plural or abstract form of hokhmah. Wisdom personified as a woman (feminine noun) who speaks publicly.

— EMET
